claim: NASA selected a Phase I concept coupling electromagnetic metamaterial design with robotic assembly for large low-CSWaP space apertures.

provenance.source_title: Robotically Assembled Electromagnetic Metamaterials for Long-Range Space Situational Awareness
limitations: NIAC concept rather than flight hardware.
Large assembled apertures occupy a different scale and role than 10 mm SNS nodes.
Assembly, calibration, structural error, and control-power budgets remain open.
provenance.fact_summary: NASA describes a concept using validated dipole and full-wave design methods together with robotic assembly heritage to explore large electromagnetic apertures for space situational awareness.
provenance.inference_summary: SNS metasurface models should include assembly topology, calibration error, support mass, and control-power costs alongside electromagnetic gain.
provenance.speculation_summary: SNS scouts may serve as distributed calibration or sensing motes around larger assembled apertures rather than forming those apertures themselves.
